source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Durham campus, two buildings coded DUR1 and DUR2, publishes 40 MW of IT capacity across 420,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 40 MW of IT load is roughly 1,000 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, the same power supports roughly 4,000 racks. The operator publishes no certifications for this campus, so no Tier rating or compliance designation can be read from the available data.

The 420,000 square feet works out to an average of about 95 watts per square foot of technical space at full IT load, which is a moderate density, consistent with a mixed-use colocation campus rather than a purpose-built high-density AI training facility. No information about power redundancy architecture, cooling technology, or fiber connectivity is published on the spec page this site has read.

Within North Carolina, this campus ranks first by published IT capacity, and it accounts for all 40 MW of published capacity in the state across this site's data. That ranking is an artifact of sparse disclosure: 19 facilities are mapped in North Carolina, but only this one has published a megawatt figure to this site. The campus's position at the top of the state ranking reflects the absence of published data from the other 18 mapped facilities, not necessarily its dominance of actual installed capacity in North Carolina.
